correctness_fixes_2026_10_27.summary: Every prior GPU decode bench of Llama-3.1-8B Q4_K_M on this card produced all-NaN logits at full speed; bench-real-model never inspected outputs (decode feeds a constant token). Found via the new NaN-tolerant logits fingerprint + TEMPURA_DEBUG_NAN per-op trace. A second fix round (same day) was found by the batch fresh-cache replay; all numbers in this file are post-both-rounds and verified.
correctness_fixes_2026_10_27.bug_1_fused_silu_format: has_sm120_fused_silu() lacked the !uses_raw_gguf gate its sm_80 sibling documents; the sm120 fused gate+up+SiLU kernel parses repacked 42-u32 but was fed native 36-u32 weights -> every block misparsed + reads past tensor end. First NaN: L0 gate-silu, 12262/14336. Fixed by gating; porting the kernel to native format is follow-up work.
correctness_fixes_2026_10_27.bug_2_cpasync_visibility: q6k_gemv_sm120_mbar_kpar8/batch: cp.async.wait_group is a PER-THREAD wait; no barrier after it, so lanes read smem words copied by other lanes before landing (word 0 is raw f32 bits -> NaN). 1-6/14336 NaN varying per run. Fixed with CTA bar.sync 0 after each wait (canonical pattern); host selects the mbar kernel only when k_blocks % 8 == 0 (uniform barrier counts -> no deadlock).

second_round_batch_replay.a_batch_kernel_m2_hardcoded: q6k_gemv_sm120_batch had 2 accumulators (M=2 hardcoded) but launched for every m>1; rows 2..M held stale memory. Rewritten as a generalized M-row two-phase kernel (phase 1: cp.async ALL weight blocks into dynamic smem; phase 2: per row-pair compute with k-split across warps).
second_round_batch_replay.b_mxfp4_padding_rows: quantize_activation ran with m_pad=16 while only m rows are valid; the m16k32 tile-max UE8M0 scale is shared by all 16 rows, so stale rows (and OOB reads past the [m*inter] silu buffer) poisoned the scale for valid rows (the M=4 all-NaN). Fixed with m_valid predicated loads + zeroed padding nibbles on the GPU kernel, CPU reference, and all five engine call sites.
second_round_batch_replay.c_m1_fallback: the old no-graph m=1 batch fallback (16 tok/s, nondeterministic NaNs) is no longer reachable; m=1 routes to the verified single-seq forward() path.
second_round_batch_replay.d_frozen_position_rope: cuTile flash-attn kv_len + cutile rope pos were HOST launch scalars baked at graph-capture time and replayed stale -- every replay after the first rotated Q/K at the capture-time position. Determinism+NaN verification cannot catch this class. Fixed by device-scalar indirection: d2d_gather_row PTX kernel copies the rope cos/sin row indexed by the position read from d_positions at execution time; graph paths require oxide_decode_attn (reads kv_len from device).
second_round_batch_replay.third_round_store_mapping: The mxf4 GEMM's hand-derived m16n8 accumulator store mapping was wrong (row = lane%16 + 8*(j/2) wrote up to 7 rows past every m16 tile into the cudaMallocAsync pool -- silent neighbor corruption at small grids, CUDA error 700 at ~896+ blocks; columns 4-7 never written). Misdiagnosed for a day as a cutlass-mlir block-count miscompile; compute-sanitizer showed writes at correct C-relative offsets landing past the C allocation, pointing at the store mapping. Fixed with the canonical mma_frag::acc_coords mapping (row = lane/4 + 8*(j>>1), col = 2*(lane%4) + (j&1)), validated by a random-data CPU-reference test in tools/mxf4-gemv. Uniform-data tests cannot catch fragment-mapping bugs: any store permutation passes, NaN comparisons are false. Every MXFP4 batch-decode output M>=2 computed before this fix is retracted; M=16 batch throughput rose 372 -> 444 tok/s from the corrected store loop.
second_round_batch_replay.e_silu_private_stream: CutileElementwise launched the SiLU kernel on a PRIVATE stream while producers/consumers ran on the matmul stream with no events -- allocation-layout-dependent race. silu_mul_device(_scratch) now take the caller's stream.
second_round_batch_replay.f_gate_up_aliasing: gemm_q4k_d2d_slot's kpar branch returned the SHARED q8_out_scratch: gate and up projections wrote the same buffer and silu computed silu(up)*up -- the single-seq FFN was mathematically wrong. kpar GEMVs now write per-slot pool tensors; pool misses fall back to the fresh-output oxide f32 GEMV.
